title: Pinned control-plane key set (agent-arena-pinned-keys/1)
description: (2.11.0) The public keys an open release trusts for hosted documents, bundled into the release (the CLI ships it as packages/arena-cli/src/hosted/pinned-keys.json). Normative text: signing.md §3.3 (what is pinned, use, the key window, rotation, `verify --key pinned`). Two sets, each exactly the body the control plane serves at `<source>?purpose=manifest` and `?purpose=report`: the manifest set is the only trust anchor for run manifests and scenario packs; the report set is what `verify --key pinned` selects from. Public keys only. The run-token key is never bundled (a run-token verifier takes it as configuration, signing.md §10), so the file has no third set. The runner never fetches keys and never takes a key from a manifest, a pack, the environment or (while a set is pinned) a flag. Rules beyond JSON Schema, checked by contracts/tools/contract-check.mjs §15 on the example and on the file the CLI bundles: each set's body reproduces its source_sha256; each set's source is the file's source plus ?purpose=<set>; kids unique across the file and no public key in both sets; every window 0 < not_after - not_before <= 120 days and revoked_at not before not_before; every kid equals its derivation from the RFC 7638 thumbprint, and sixi_thumbprint (when present) equals that thumbprint; x is a canonical 32-byte key.

source.description: The published JWKS URL, without query. Since 2026-09-27: https://sixi.ch/.well-known/arena-jwks.json.

fetched_at.description: When the release process fetched both sets.

source_etag.description: Informative: the ETag of the unfiltered JWKS response.

source_sha256.description: Informative: sha256 of the unfiltered JWKS body, which also lists the run-token key and so cannot be reproduced from this file.

note.description: Informative text for readers of the file. Never read by a verifier.

manifest.description: The ?purpose=manifest JWKS body, stored as served: UTF-8(JSON.stringify({"keys": keys}) + LF) hashes to source_sha256.

source_sha256.description: sha256 of the exact served body.

keys.description: 1..16 keys. Kids unique across the file, and no public key (x) in both sets.

report.description: The ?purpose=report JWKS body, stored as served: UTF-8(JSON.stringify({"keys": keys}) + LF) hashes to source_sha256.

source_sha256.description: sha256 of the exact served body.

keys.description: 1..16 keys. Kids unique across the file, and no public key (x) in both sets.

jwk.description: One public key as the JWKS serves it (signing.md §3.3 rule 1). Only the members below; a private member such as `d` makes the file invalid (additionalProperties). The window [not_before, not_after), cut short by revoked_at, is the only time a key verifies (rule 3).

x.description: The 32-byte Ed25519 public key, canonical unpadded base64url (43 characters, decoding to 32 bytes and re-encoding to the same string).

kid.description: The key id: `<namespace>-ed25519-` + the first 80 bits of the RFC 7638 thumbprint in lower-case hex (signing.md §3.3 rule 1). The set narrows the namespace.

sixi_purpose.description: When present, equal to the set that holds the key.

status.description: The control plane's rotation state when fetched. Informational: it never widens or narrows the window.

not_before.description: Inclusive start of the window, RFC 3339 UTC with seconds and `Z`.

not_after.description: Exclusive end of the window. not_after - not_before is at most 120 days (90 days of use + 30 days of overlap); contract-check §15.

revoked_at.description: When present, the window ends here (exclusive) if that is before not_after.

sixi_thumbprint.description: When present, the full RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of {crv, kty, x}, base64url. The kid is derived from it.

examples.note: Public keys only. manifest = ?purpose=manifest, report = ?purpose=report, each kept exactly as served (JSON.stringify(set) + LF reproduces the served body, whose sha256 is recorded). The run-token key is not bundled: the CLI never verifies a run token with a pinned key (serve-reference --hosted takes --run-token-key). Rotation: a new key ships in an open release before the control plane first signs with it; keys have a 90-day window, so at least one open release per quarter.
